content: 1. All individuals diagnosed with diabetes should be actively encouraged to participate in Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) programs. These programs are designed to enhance their ability to make informed decisions, adopt effective self-care behaviors, solve problems related to their condition, and collaborate effectively with their healthcare teams. 2. The need for DSMES should be reassessed on an annual basis to ensure that individuals with diabetes continue to strengthen their skills in implementing treatment plans and maintaining effective collaboration with healthcare providers. 3. The primary objectives of DSMES include improving clinical outcomes, enhancing overall health status, and promoting well-being. These outcomes should be routinely evaluated as an integral part of comprehensive diabetes care. 4. DSMES programs must be culturally sensitive and tailored to align with the individual’s preferences, needs, and values. These programs can be delivered in either group settings or one-on-one sessions. Furthermore, all education and support provided should be thoroughly documented and made accessible to the entire diabetes care team. 5. Consider offering DSMES through telehealth services or digital platforms to minimize barriers to access and improve patient satisfaction with the care provided. 6. It is recommended that third-party payers provide reimbursement for DSMES, as evidence demonstrates that these programs lead to improved health outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. 7. Efforts should be made to identify and address barriers to DSMES at multiple levels, including those related to payers, healthcare systems, clinics, healthcare professionals, and individual patients. 8. When planning and delivering DSMES, it is essential to take into account the social determinants of health to ensure equitable health outcomes across diverse populations.
